title: Graph Attention Networks (GAT)
interviewAnswer: GAT learns attention weights over neighbors so different neighbors contribute differently instead of using fixed aggregation weights.
keyPoints: Attention is local over graph neighbors.
why: Graph Attention Networks (GAT) is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: Attention is local over graph neighbors.
deepDive: GAT learns attention weights over neighbors so different neighbors contribute differently instead of using fixed aggregation weights. Multi-head attention can stabilize/expand representations. More flexible aggregation costs compute. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: In a fraud graph, learn to emphasize suspicious transaction neighbors more than benign high-degree neighbors.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Graph Attention Networks (GAT)?
How would you validate or tune Graph Attention Networks (GAT)?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
